source: Original (freshly authored 2026-10-05, AA SL 4.2, calculator allowed). Cumulative frequency curve of homework time t (0-120 minutes) for 100 students, drawn through (0,0) (10,2) (20,7) (30,15) (40,25) (50,37) (60,50) (70,63) (80,75) (90,84) (100,90) (110,96) (120,100). Q1=40, median=60, Q3=80, IQR=40; 85 students at least 30 minutes; 90th percentile at 100 minutes; min 5, max 118, fences -20 and 140, no outliers.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Use the cumulative frequency graph of homework times for 100 students to write down the median time.
parts.notes: A1 for the reading at cumulative frequency 50.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find the interquartile range of the homework times.
parts.tolerance: Accept Q1 in 39 to 41 and Q3 in 79 to 81; IQR consistent with the student's quartiles.
parts.notes: A1 for both quartiles (read at cumulative frequencies 25 and 75). A1 for IQR = Q3 - Q1, FT from the student's quartiles. Quartiles read at other cumulative frequencies earn A0A0.

parts.label: c
parts.description: Find the number of students who spent at least 30 minutes on homework.
parts.notes: (M1) for reading the curve at t = 30 (15), seen or implied by a line on the graph. A1 for 100 - 15 = 85. A final answer of 15 earns M1A0.

parts.label: d
parts.description: The 10% of students who spent the most time on homework are invited to a workshop. Find the least time that an invited student spent on homework.

expected.method: 90% of 100 = 90; read the curve at cumulative frequency 90

parts.notes: (M1) for reading at cumulative frequency 90, seen or implied by a line on the graph. A1 for 100. Reading at cumulative frequency 10 (about 24 minutes) earns M0A0.

parts.label: e
parts.description: The shortest time was 5 minutes and the longest was 118 minutes. Show that there are no outliers in the data.
parts.tolerance: Boundaries FT from the student's quartiles and IQR in part (b).
parts.notes: M1 for at least one boundary correctly calculated. R1 for both comparisons, with the minimum and the maximum. AG: the conclusion. Checking only the longest time earns M1R0.
parts.follow_through: Boundaries use Q1, Q3 and IQR from part (b); award M1R1 for correct boundaries and comparisons from the student's own (b) values.

answer_box_top_frac_note: The answer box runs 0.630 to 0.938. source: Original (freshly authored 2026-10-05, AA SL 4.2 and 4.3, calculator allowed). Cumulative frequency curve of the masses m (100-200 g) of 120 apples, drawn through (100,0) (110,3) (120,10) (130,20) (140,35) (150,55) (160,75) (170,90) (180,105) (190,114) (200,120). Grouped table with classes of width 20: frequencies 10, 25, p, q, 15 with p=40, q=30. Median 152.5 g; 30 apples over 170 g; estimated mean 18300/120 = 152.5 g.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Use the cumulative frequency graph of the masses of 120 apples to estimate the median mass.
parts.notes: A1 for the reading at cumulative frequency 60 (or 60.5).

parts.label: b
parts.description: Apples with a mass of more than 170 grams are graded 'large'. Find the number of large apples.
parts.notes: (M1) for reading the curve at m = 170 (90), seen or implied by a line on the graph. A1 for 120 - 90 = 30. A final answer of 90 earns M1A0.

parts.label: c
parts.description: Use the graph to find p, the frequency of 140 < m <= 160, and q, the frequency of 160 < m <= 180.
parts.tolerance: Accept values consistent with readings within 1 of 35, 75 and 105 at m = 140, 160, 180.
parts.notes: A1 for p = 75 - 35 = 40. A1 for q = 105 - 75 = 30. Check: 10 + 25 + 40 + 30 + 15 = 120. Cumulative frequencies given as frequencies (p = 75, q = 105) earn A0A0.

parts.label: d
parts.description: Find an estimate of the mean mass of the apples, using the grouped frequency table.
parts.tolerance: FT from the student's p and q.
parts.notes: (M1) for using mid-interval values with the frequencies (GDC One-Variable Statistics with a frequency list is acceptable working). A1 for 152.5. Class boundaries instead of mid-interval values, or the plain mean of the five mid-interval values (150), earn M0A0.
parts.follow_through: Uses p and q from part (c); award A1 for the correct mean from the student's own p and q with mid-interval values.

parts.label: e
parts.description: Explain why the answer to part (d) is an estimate.

expected.answer: The actual masses are not known; each apple is given the mid-interval value of its class.

parts.tolerance: Accept 'the data are grouped', 'mid-interval values are used'.
parts.notes: R1 for the grouped data / mid-interval reason. 'The graph is not exact' alone earns R0.
